$comment: P4.D152 — the shared corpus for v4's REAL `realign-file-entry-sha256-v1` migration (v4 `0b0617fee`, bug 117) and v5's `db::files_sha256_realign_heal`. `files` rows are the MAIN partition; `blobs` are `doc_mount_blobs` in the MOUNT partition. `generate` synthesises N agreeing-id pairs whose file sha is always drifted, for the past-the-first-batch scenario (v4 BATCH_SIZE = 500).

scenarios.name: drifted-row-realigned
scenarios.$comment: The shape bug 117 wrote: files.sha256 is the PRE-transcode hash, the blob carries the stored one.

scenarios.name: agreeing-row-untouched
scenarios.$comment: Already in agreement: skipped, and updatedAt must NOT move. v4's runner still records a zero-itemsAffected ledger row here (shouldRun tests presence, not drift) — v5 records nothing; the divergence is pinned by the ledger comparand.

scenarios.name: missing-blob-left-alone
scenarios.$comment: The blob has gone; the row is counted orphaned, warned about, and left as it is rather than guessed at.

scenarios.name: malformed-key-batch-continues
scenarios.$comment: `mount-blob:mp-1:` has sep === rest.length - 1 → refused; `mount-blob::b-0002` has sep < 1 → refused. The rows AFTER them still realign, which is the point.

scenarios.name: non-mount-blob-rows-ignored
scenarios.$comment: A legacy disk key and a NULL storageKey are never selected by the LIKE, so they are not even scanned.

scenarios.name: no-mount-blob-rows-at-all
scenarios.$comment: v4's shouldRun() is false — the runner SKIPS and records nothing. v5 returns NoDrift{scanned:0} and records nothing. The one arm where the two ledgers agree on silence.

scenarios.name: ledger-row-present-skips-the-drift
scenarios.$comment: A migrations_state row is already there (v4 having run its own migration on a shared instance). v4's runner refuses at isMigrationCompleted; v5's heal refuses at the same check. The row IS drifted, so a heal that ignored the ledger would realign it and the arm would redden.

scenarios.name: past-the-first-batch
scenarios.$comment: 507 drifted rows — one full batch of 500 plus seven. The keyset walk must pass the first batch; batching is otherwise unobservable by state (see the family header).
